results.content:
Two changes would shift our answer. If Plaud publishes open-source firmware, Omi's developer edge would shrink. If Omi introduces a mid-tier subscription priced near $100 per year, Plaud's price edge would shrink.

## The Verdict

The Plaud NotePin is the best all-around alternative to Omi for mainstream professionals. At $159 for the device, it matches Omi's 300 free monthly minutes and offers a 1,200-minute Pro tier for $99.99 a year. This makes Plaud cheaper for moderate monthly workloads than Omi Unlimited at about $270 per year. [...] - The primary hardware alternatives to Omi are the Plaud NotePin ($159), the Fieldy 3 ($129 on sale), and the Bee Pioneer ($49.99). Users who conduct meetings primarily at desks can also use software-based meeting recorders to capture computer audio directly without buying wearable hardware.
- Plaud NotePin is the most practical choice for business professionals needing up to 1,200 minutes of notes per month due to its $99.99 annual plan. Omi is the top choice for developers who require open-source code and MCP server integrations.
- For a dedicated device, we would pick Plaud NotePin or Omi. Plaud provides structured tiers for moderate workloads, while Omi provides an open-source MIT codebase, on-phone processing, and an app marketplace with over 1,000 extensions. [...] Are you one of these vendors?Update your listing

## The Short List of Omi Alternatives

Plaud NotePin, Fieldy 3 and Bee are the three wearable recorders to compare with Omi. Limitless no longer sells its Pendant.

Plaud is the closest direct competitor on meeting minute tiers. Its Plaud NotePin costs $159 and matches Omi's 300 free monthly minutes. It also sells a middle-tier plan for $99.99 a year with 1,200 minutes per month.

Fieldy provides the lowest subscription cost for unlimited transcription. Field Labs Inc. sells the Fieldy 3 for $129 on sale, and its unlimited tier costs $191.88 a year billed annually.

Bee provides the cheapest hardware entry point at $49.99. Bee was acquired by Amazon, operates exclusively on iOS, and ships only to addresses within the United States.

### The app is the problem, not the pendant

Keep the Omi. Fluent pairs with it and turns what it hears into meeting notes, the commitments people made, profiles of the people you talk to, and coaching.

### You don't want a pendant at all

For meetings, your phone may be enough: Fluent records a meeting straight from your iPhone, so there is no device to buy.

## Questions

### What is the best alternative to Omi?

If you want a different device, Plaud NotePin ($159) is the most finished alternative in stock. If you like the Omi hardware but not its app, keep it and use Fluent with it.

### Can I still buy a Limitless or Bee pendant? [...] # Fluent vs Omi: same pendant,different software.

Omi is an open-source pendant. Fluent is closed-source software that runs on top of it. They don't compete. They're stacked on each other.

If you bought an Omi, you can have both. Most early adopters do.

## What you're actually choosing between

### Omi (the pendant + native app)

- Open-source hardware. Hackable. Light.
- Open-source app.
- Community of developers building plugins.
- The full stack if you want to tinker.

### Fluent (software for your Omi)

- Polished iOS app. Native feel.
- Meeting notes written like a chief of staff wrote them.
- Person profiles. Calendar agent. Coach. Daily insights.
- MCP server for plugging into Claude or ChatGPT.

Choose Omi when the wearable is central and you want a personal assistant spanning conversations, memories, reminders, tasks, and proactive nudges. Choose screenpipe when you want searchable work memory, a durable second brain, reports and SOPs from real activity, or agents that automate repeated computer workflows.
